news.title: 165,000 people call for Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia
news.description: Elon Musk and more than 165,000 people have signed an open letter asking Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as its leader. More than 7,500 signatories identified themselves as Nvidia employees.

news.title: Apple launches study on trust in medical AI
news.description: Apple has launched a one-year study with clinical tool OpenEvidence to understand what inspires trust in healthcare chatbots and whether users understand their answers. Up to 200,000 Americans can participate, subject to certain hardware and software requirements.

news.title: SpaceX completes first catch of an orbit-returning Starship
news.description: On Saturday, SpaceX caught its Starship spacecraft with the mechanical arms of its launch tower in Texas. The spacecraft released 26 Starlink satellites and completed 14 orbits of Earth, but the Super Heavy booster exploded during its descent.

news.title: Apple’s Siri AI glasses could launch next year
news.description: Apple is reportedly preparing to launch smart glasses equipped with Siri and AI features next year.

news.title: GPT-6 Astra helps demonstrate a mathematical construction of the Standard Model
news.description: OpenAI and physicist Nathaniel Craig have published a candidate lattice construction of the Standard Model. GPT-6 Astra reportedly contributed to its development and demonstration.

news.title: Failed launch destroys 40 Amazon Leo satellites
news.description: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket failed about ten minutes after liftoff, destroying 40 satellites intended for Amazon Leo. The failure occurred during ignition of the Centaur upper stage, whose cause remains unknown.

news.title: Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic could become AI “national champions”
news.description: The Trump administration is reportedly considering designating Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic as “national champions” of artificial intelligence.

news.title: Microsoft outage takes down 80% of servers
news.description: A Microsoft outage caused 80% of servers to shut down. The article explains what happened.

news.title: Papa John’s uses AI to reduce pizza inconsistencies
news.description: Papa John’s is turning to artificial intelligence to tackle variations in how its pizzas are prepared.

news.title: Two HPE Juniper routers ground all U.S. flights
news.description: Two HPE Juniper network routers caused all flights in the United States to be grounded on Friday.

news.title: A five-step method to stop ChatGPT from making promises on your behalf
news.description: ChatGPT tends to answer yes to implicit requests in an email, sometimes inventing deadlines or commitments. The recommended method is to extract the requests, answer yes, no or not yet, then draft and audit the response.

news.title: OpenAI explains GPT-4o’s overly agreeable behavior
news.description: A 2025 update made ChatGPT excessively agreeable, leading OpenAI to roll it back.

news.title: Google unveils smart glasses with a camera and Gemini
news.description: Google unveiled Intelligent Eyewear, glasses that let users ask Gemini about what they see, take hands-free photos and videos, and translate conversations. They feature a 12-megapixel ultra-wide-angle camera and can share the wearer’s view live in a Google Meet call.

news.title: Claude Meetings arrives in beta for Google Meet calls
news.description: Anthropic launched Claude Meetings in beta, allowing Claude to join Google Meet calls on Team and Enterprise plans. The assistant can take notes, answer questions, and begin creating documents and whiteboards.

news.title: Embedded browser works on a 2015 Tesla Model S
news.description: A user says that the map and globe work in the built-in browser of their 2015 Model S, although using them is not particularly practical.

news.title: OpenAI rolls out ChatGPT Wallet to let agents make payments
news.description: ChatGPT Wallet, developed with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, lets agents make payments by replacing card details with a token. The rollout begins on Dots for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the United States.

news.title: Nvidia’s decline puts Asian chipmakers to the test
news.description: Nvidia’s downturn is putting pressure on players in the Asian artificial-intelligence trade, from TSMC to SK Hynix.

news.title: GTA VI and Anthropic’s IPO arrive on the same day
news.description: The release of Grand Theft Auto VI and Anthropic’s stock-market debut are scheduled for the same Thursday, in a rare cultural and economic collision. Anthropic could reach a valuation of 1 400 billion dollars and raise up to 90 billion.

news.title: Anthropic’s IPO will be a major test for AI
news.description: Anthropic’s stock-market debut will be the first major test of investor appetite for a company devoted entirely to artificial intelligence.

news.title: GTA VI’s success could support the video game industry
news.description: Amid threats from artificial intelligence and high hardware costs, GTA VI’s success could help maintain player engagement with other games.

news.title: The 9-billion-dollar foundation created by Nvidia’s boom
news.description: Nvidia’s artificial-intelligence boom has helped create a 9-billion-dollar foundation led by Lori Huang. The article details how the funds are being used.

news.title: Samsung reportedly approached Anthropic and OpenAI to lease its future AI data centers
news.description: Samsung’s IT division has reportedly begun talks with Anthropic and OpenAI about becoming tenants of its future artificial intelligence data centers.

news.title: A compromised MCP server can hijack an AI agent’s other tools
news.description: A test cited by VentureBeat found that a compromised MCP server could prompt an agent connected to five servers to misuse the other tools in 78.3% of cases. The article recommends limiting credentials, adding human approvals, and logging the entire call chain.

news.title: The Atlantic tests ChatGPT on 32,245 personal messages and raises consent questions
news.description: The Atlantic tested ChatGPT on 32,245 personal messages. The experiment raises consent questions when an analysis conducted for one person includes other people’s private conversations.

news.title: Nvidia’s board is not considering Jensen Huang’s return
news.description: Support for Jensen Huang’s return is growing inside and outside Nvidia. However, a person familiar with the board’s position confirmed to Business Insider that it is not considering reinstating him as CEO.

news.title: A guide to cleanly transferring AI work into your documents
news.description: Chapter 31 of AI Bootcamp explains how to choose the destination format before asking AI for help, then how to export or copy the work without losing its formatting. It also recommends three checks before sharing the result: read everything, be able to explain every fact, and follow the team’s format.

news.title: U.S. blocks overseas leasing of Chinese AI chips
news.description: The Trump administration is introducing new export controls to prevent Chinese companies from remotely accessing AI chips and data centers located in other countries. The rule will require licenses for infrastructure capable of providing more than 12 million TPP.

news.title: Alibaba says Qwen4-Max cuts task costs by 62%
news.description: According to Alibaba’s Work360 benchmark, the Qwen4-Max model performs professional tasks for 62% less than the previous version, with average costs falling from $4.43 to $1.67. The model activates fewer parameters per token and uses 35% fewer tokens.

news.title: AI tools can now find zero-day vulnerabilities for $4
news.description: AI tools can find zero-day vulnerabilities for just $4, allowing even inexperienced hackers to exploit them.

news.title: Apple steps up its development of video podcasts
news.description: Apple is increasing its efforts in the video podcast space.

news.title: Top Korean candidate in tax exam admits cheating with AI
news.description: The candidate who ranked first in South Korea on a notoriously difficult tax exam admitted to using AI to cheat.

news.title: Italy fines Meta €805 million over access to Android photos
news.description: Italy has fined Meta €805 million over Facebook’s access to photos stored on Android devices.

news.title: Google Maps creates routes with real-time information
news.description: Google Maps can now create routes that include real-time information about each leg of the journey.

news.title: Judge allows DRAM price-fixing lawsuit to proceed
news.description: A judge rejected a motion to dismiss a lawsuit against Micron, Samsung and SK hynix. The judge found plausible the evidence suggesting a DRAM price-fixing conspiracy after prices rose by 500%.

news.title: Camera attacks disrupt autonomous vehicle tracking
news.description: Camera attacks can fool an autonomous car’s vehicle-tracking system by subtly altering its video feed. Tracking accuracy can thus drop from about 55% to 15% or lower.

news.title: Mass adoption of AI video tools could increase their emissions 75-fold
news.description: Emissions from AI video tools could increase nearly 75-fold by 2030 if their growth continues despite efficiency gains. Keeping usage at its current level would reduce emissions by about two-fifths.

news.title: Medical AI spending reaches $3.7 billion
news.description: Spending on AI in healthcare increased 2.5-fold to $3.7 billion in 2026, surpassing the legal and financial sectors combined. The market is shifting from note-taking to complex clinical workflows and drug discovery.

news.title: Study examines why users reward agreeable responses
news.description: The study finds that users tend to value pleasant responses, which may explain why model-generated drafts drift toward systematic approval.

news.title: Gmail offers templates for saving reusable replies
news.description: Gmail’s guide explains how to save a reusable message, which can be used to retain an email-writing prompt.

news.title: Outlook lets users reuse text blocks with Quick Parts
news.description: Outlook’s guide introduces Quick Parts, a feature that lets users save and reuse text blocks.

news.title: Claude adds whiteboards, spreadsheets and dashboards
news.description: Anthropic has added workspaces to Claude for jointly creating spreadsheets, whiteboards and dashboards. Claude can also turn data into visual stories or short narrated videos, while Claude Motion is available in beta.

news.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen lets users adjust the reasoning level
news.description: Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a model designed for everyday coding and agentic tasks, available worldwide since November 12. It offers four reasoning levels — low, medium, high and xhigh — to balance quality, speed and cost, with a context window of up to one million tokens.

news.title: Grok Bot reaches version 1.0 and becomes an autonomous teammate
news.description: SpaceXAI upgraded Grok Bot to version 1.0. The bot can handle tasks without prompting and maintain shared memory within an organization in Slack and Microsoft Teams.

news.title: Claude Code tutorial helps beginners without programming skills
news.description: Kevin published a Claude Code tutorial for people who do not code. It is presented as a starting point for creating a first project without writing the code themselves.

news.title: Tesla invites some users to order the Cybercab
news.description: Some people are reportedly receiving invitations to order a Cybercab. The vehicle would cost 30 000 dollars, require a 300-dollar-per-month FSD subscription, and operate only within a limited geofenced area.

news.title: An app update could provide one free month of FSD
news.description: Two users were able to receive one free month of FSD after updating their Tesla app.

news.title: The Tesla Mobile Connector could receive updates through the car
news.description: Users report charging stopping with the Mobile Connector and mention updates to the connector being delivered through the car.

news.title: Tesla software version 38.5.13 could bring major changes
news.description: A user says they upgraded from version 38.5.12 to 38.5.13 and announces major changes to come.

news.title: User asks why their Tesla has not received an update yet
news.description: A discussion thread seeks the reasons why a Tesla vehicle has not yet received a software update.

news.title: Speed profiles could help FSD handle certain limitations better
news.description: According to one participant, higher speed profiles could help FSD when an incorrect speed limit causes it to drive too slowly, allowing it to adapt better to traffic.

news.title: Delivery of a Model Y Performance ordered in September is delayed
news.description: A buyer of a Quicksilver Model Y Performance ordered on September 5 still has not received a VIN and is seeing the delivery dates pushed back.

news.title: Discussion focuses on the shape of Tesla jack pads
news.description: A user says the jack pads they have seen are flat, while a non-flat base could reduce the risk of slipping if it fits the jack point properly.

news.title: Tesla navigation reportedly suggested inconsistent routes during an air-traffic disruption
news.description: A user claims that their Tesla’s navigation system became inconsistent when the FAA had ordered all aircraft to remain grounded, and asks whether others noticed unusual routes.

news.title: Bland AI introduces Tofu-1, a voice model that generates soundscapes
news.description: Tofu-1 combines multiple voices, overlapping conversations and background noises. Bland AI says that 92% of listeners did not identify the model as AI.

news.title: Microsoft and the FAA deny any link between their outages and AI
news.description: Microsoft attributes its Outlook outage to a technical issue related to a network-capacity upgrade. The FAA explains the grounding of air traffic as the result of a project to modernize its communications, while rumors continue to implicate AI.

news.title: Greg Isenberg lists 49 uses of AI in business
news.description: Entrepreneur Greg Isenberg published a list of 49 ways to use AI in an organization. His post received nearly 15 000 saves.

news.title: Mainframe founder describes his workday with AI agents
news.description: The co-founder of Mainframe says he now works in short bursts spread throughout the day. He also asks his agents to continue certain tasks overnight.

news.title: Claude Code lets users customize its interface theme
news.description: Claude Code now lets users replace its black or white themes with customized colors and animations.

news.title: Claude improves multitasking for large projects
news.description: Another Claude update improves its multitasking capabilities during major projects.

news.title: Lessons from Rubrik on cloud resilience and business recovery
news.description: At Rubrik’s Cloud Resilience Summit 2026, Pascal Bornet examines the recovery of the data, code and applications needed to run a business. He particularly emphasizes the importance of defining the “Minimum Viable Business” to restore after an attack.

news.title: Microsoft raises cloud prices in India and New Zealand
news.description: Microsoft will increase prices for its commercial cloud by 15.7% in India and 10% in New Zealand starting January 1, 2027, citing currency adjustments. Prices will fall in China, Australia and Norway, while some on-premises products will increase by up to 20% in India.

news.title: AI recovery requires more than a simple undo button
news.description: Restoring an AI agent, undoing its changes in internal systems, and neutralizing their business consequences are three distinct problems. Commvault’s recovery tools address part of the first two, but some actions require controls before execution.

news.title: AWS Secrets Manager supports cross-account replication
news.description: AWS Secrets Manager now supports cross-account replication, allowing synchronized copies of primary secrets to be maintained for backup, disaster recovery, and cross-account access. The feature extends multi-Region replication across account boundaries.

news.title: Nvidia, AMD, Google, and Meta join open inference consortium
news.description: LMSYS launched the SGLang Consortium to coordinate engineering work on its open-source AI inference engine, with Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Google, and Meta among its founding members. Members will contribute deployment feedback, testing, and development, while SGLang maintainers will retain control over technical decisions.

news.title: An architecture for creating always-on agents
news.description: The architecture for always-on agents is built around five core primitives: an event inbox, persistent timers, persistent memory, a permissions system, and an outbound communications box. It is designed to let AI agents operate autonomously in the background while maintaining state and proactive behavior.

news.title: Marvell targets AI bottlenecks tied to memory and networking
news.description: Marvell is showcasing optical interconnects, CXL memory expansion, and networking technologies at Supercomputing 2026. The demonstrations focus on scaling memory and compute across racks to address bandwidth constraints and infrastructure underutilization.

news.title: Cloudflare introduces private origins for its application services
news.description: Cloudflare’s Private Origins connect public Internet traffic to private applications without exposing their IP addresses or opening inbound ports on firewalls.

news.title: GitHub Copilot app supports Enterprise Server
news.description: Support for GitHub Enterprise Server is now generally available in version 1.2.0 and later of the Copilot app.

news.title: GitHub will schedule the removal of Copilot models in December
news.description: GitHub will retire six selected Copilot models on December 14.

news.title: Marathon Fusion claims to have created gold from mercury
news.description: Fusion startup Marathon Fusion claims to have produced gold from mercury. It did not disclose how much was produced, and its process requires a fusion power plant that does not yet exist.

news.title: The essential steps in creating a programming language
news.description: A compiler progressively transforms text into tokens and then into a tree, before verification and execution by an interpreter or the production of a native binary. The main challenge is making errors useful and maintaining consistency between the two backends.

news.title: Persistent agents manage their context and act without supervision
news.description: Persistent agents operate indefinitely, manage their context across sessions, and take action without direct supervision. They are becoming more practical thanks to advances in models, better judgment, and the falling cost of intelligence.

news.title: Remote work could weigh on employment for recent graduates
news.description: Recent graduates are less employed than they were a few years ago. AI could play a role, but the data also suggests that remote work strongly affects their employment, with the two factors difficult to distinguish.

news.title: Advances in mathematics could accelerate AI research
news.description: AI systems’ mathematical abilities have advanced rapidly, and they can now easily solve well-defined problems. This capability could be even more important for machine-learning research than for mathematics itself.

news.title: Trend extrapolation places AGI one to four years away
news.description: An extrapolation of current trends estimates that AGI far exceeding human capabilities could emerge within one to four years. If recursive self-improvement has begun, that timeline could be six to eighteen months.

news.title: Tesla opens preorders for personal Cybercab at $299 per month
news.description: Some customers can now preorder the gold Cybercab for $29,990, with geographic restrictions. First deliveries are estimated for December, and the offering includes a $299 monthly subscription.

news.title: Analysis distinguishes the three components of recursive self-improvement
news.description: The article separates the three components of recursive self-improvement and shows that the deep-learning paradigm forces researchers to define what constitutes the improved “self.”

news.title: AI is disrupting hiring processes for employees and employers
news.description: AI is overwhelming processes that require public input, causing them to malfunction.

news.title: China fires researchers after child dies during trial
news.description: Researchers failed to report warning signs from a study involving nonhuman primates. They also did not disclose the child’s death in the published scientific paper.

news.title: The intelligence case against Jensen Huang could be weak
news.description: Alistair Barr examines why the intelligence allegations against Jensen Huang may lack substance.

news.title: Should Jensen Huang return to his position if doubts are confirmed?
news.description: Jamie Heller considers whether Jensen Huang should return to his position if doubts about the intelligence case are justified.

news.title: Madison Huang was gaining influence at Nvidia, but may not be ready
news.description: Madison Huang had increased her influence within Nvidia. Former colleagues, however, believe she is not ready to replace her father.

news.title: Jensen Huang’s downfall puts the founder cult to the test
news.description: Jensen Huang’s downfall is testing the “founder cult,” described as one of the most powerful religions in the United States.

news.title: Nvidia engineer announces departure
news.description: An Nvidia engineer says he is leaving the company amid Jensen Huang’s downfall.

news.title: SNL turns Nvidia affair into a techie espionage lesson
news.description: “SNL” seized on the Jensen Huang affair and turned it into a techie-style espionage lesson.

news.title: GTA VI could generate $1.18 billion in preorders
news.description: GTA VI preorder estimates have reached 12.13 million copies, generating $1.18 billion in revenue, according to SensorTower.

news.title: GTA VI’s release sends time-off requests soaring
news.description: Time-off requests for GTA VI’s release week rose by about 20% compared with the same weeks in previous years. Some companies are even encouraging employees to take advantage of it.

news.title: U.S. markets retreat ahead of a pivotal week for AI
news.description: U.S. stock futures fell Monday as investors prepared for an important week for the AI sector, with Nvidia’s earnings in focus.

news.title: New Goldman Sachs partner recounts the day he was appointed
news.description: Jake Woodson, 34, recounts how he learned he was becoming one of Goldman Sachs’ youngest new partners, from celebrating with colleagues to having dinner with his mother.

news.title: S&P 500 could fall as much as 15%, strategist says
news.description: Jim Paulsen estimates that the S&P 500 could decline by as much as 15% as the technology market readjusts.

news.title: Student turns $35 into a six-figure marketing agency
news.description: Student Stavya Nilawar built a creator-marketing agency from his dorm room that generates six-figure revenue.

news.title: Developers must now learn to communicate better
news.description: Companies now expect engineers to interact directly with customers. They therefore need to learn how to communicate with nontechnical people.

news.title: Meta stock gains could free some employees from their constraints
news.description: The final vesting of stock grants awarded in 2023 is due in February, after Meta’s share price rose 400%. The increase could loosen the “golden handcuffs” keeping some employees in place.

news.title: Jensen Huang joins founders ousted from their own companies
news.description: After resigning following 33 years at Nvidia, Jensen Huang joins Steve Jobs, Elon Musk, and Sam Altman among founders who lost control of their companies.

news.title: A year of turmoil surrounding H-1B visas
news.description: In September 2025, the Trump administration imposed $100,000 fees on certain H-1B visa applications, triggering repercussions for a year. Business Insider interviewed more than 20 visa holders and applicants.

news.title: Recipients of buyout packages describe life after leaving
news.description: Nine people who accepted voluntary departures, including former Microsoft employees, share the advice they would give to those considering the option and describe their new lives.

news.title: Consumers prioritize value despite inflation
news.description: Consumers continue shopping despite persistent inflation, but are specifically seeking the best value for money. The trend is particularly pronounced among millennials.

news.title: Some ingredients should be avoided in facial cleansers
news.description: Washing your face every morning is not necessary, but certain precautions are recommended if you choose to do so, particularly regarding the ingredients used.

news.title: Parents save for a future without college
news.description: Some parents are abandoning 529 savings plans to prepare financially for their children’s future, which may not necessarily include college.

news.title: Former Google and Facebook employees share their networking methods
news.description: A person who worked at Google, Facebook, and the White House presents networking habits that can help people land a job.

news.title: Ten challenges for real estate in 2026, according to young leaders
news.description: Young leaders identify ten challenges the real estate industry is expected to face in 2026.

news.title: Bryan Johnson launches a meal service inspired by his diet
news.description: Bryan Johnson has created a meal delivery service that lets people eat like him. Nutritionists weigh in on the offering.

news.title: Wall Street’s rising stars over the past decade
news.description: Business Insider profiles Wall Street’s rising stars who have stood out over the past ten years.

news.title: Steve Hanke reveals his best investment and biggest regret
news.description: Investor Steve Hanke considers a Patek Philippe watch he bought at 16 his best investment and also shares his biggest regret.

news.title: The first AI Music Awards rely on humans to portray AI artists
news.description: The first AI Music Awards ceremony was held in Los Angeles, featuring AI presenters, lip-syncing, and human stand-ins. Technical problems interrupted the ceremony several times.

news.title: Nvidia reportedly supplied computing capacity to Chinese companies through Asia
news.description: According to The Wall Street Journal, Nvidia developed partnerships with Asian data centers that leased its advanced chips to Chinese customers. One of these partners reportedly arranged nearly 12 billion dollars’ worth of chip orders in 2024 and 2025.

news.title: Pax Silica countries seek better protection for key AI technologies and supply chains
news.description: Members of Pax Silica, including Japan, Australia, Israel, India, and the United Kingdom, agreed to establish a joint list of AI technologies and supply chains requiring greater protection.

news.title: SK Hynix to invest 1.05 billion dollars in its South Korean suppliers
news.description: SK Hynix has committed to investing approximately 1.05 billion dollars over five years to strengthen Korean suppliers of semiconductor materials, components, and equipment.

news.title: LongCat-2.5 nearly matches Claude Opus 5 without using Nvidia chips
news.description: Meituan’s Chinese model scores 88.4 on Terminal Bench, nearly matching Claude Opus 5, and was reportedly trained entirely on Huawei chips. It combines 1,600 billion parameters, a one-million-token context window, and advanced agent capabilities.

news.title: A robot independently assembles a structure in orbit
news.description: Caltech’s ASTRA robot built a section of an antenna frame in low Earth orbit without an astronaut. The DARPA-backed demonstration is intended to pave the way for much larger space structures.

news.title: Alibaba opens Qwen4-Max Preview for two weeks
news.description: Alibaba is allowing users to test Qwen4-Max Preview until November 25. The multimodal model has a one-million-token context window, agent tools, and compatibility with several development environments.

news.title: Washington prepares three bills to tighten AI chip exports to China
news.description: Following unproven allegations involving Jensen Huang, the US Congress is preparing three bills designed to strengthen restrictions on AI chips exported to China. None has yet been passed, and the details of the measures remain unknown.

news.title: A middle school student invents a water-powered solar tracker
news.description: Jason Chang designed a system costing less than 25 dollars that points a solar panel using a bucket filled by dripping water, without a motor or electricity. The device produces approximately 20% more voltage than a fixed panel.

news.title: Confucius4-R2T2 locks words in live voice transcriptions
news.description: The system locks each word as soon as it appears, without rewriting the beginning of sentences, while remaining fast and nearly as accurate as delayed transcription. It is based on an adaptation of Qwen3-ASR-1.7B trained on 1,500 hours of Chinese and English audio.

news.title: Apple runs an 816-billion-parameter model on four Mac Studio computers
news.description: The new version of MLX distributes a very large model across multiple Mac Studio computers connected via Thunderbolt. Muse Spark Open exceeds 36 tokens per second on four machines, while some models fit on a single 512 GB Mac Studio.

news.title: Alibaba releases its open-source AI code review tool
news.description: Alibaba has open-sourced open-code-review, a tool that combines conventional rules with an AI agent to comment on code line by line. It looks for XSS vulnerabilities, SQL injections, and common crashes, among other issues.

news.title: Claude Cowork lets users launch desktop tasks from a phone
news.description: Claude Cowork can sort files, turn screenshots into spreadsheets, and compile notes into a report. The computer and mobile apps work together so users can launch a task from a phone for execution on a computer.

news.title: Claude Fable 5.2 paints its images with Python code
news.description: Claude Fable 5.2 generates images by writing Python code that simulates hundreds of thousands of brushstrokes. A photorealistic parking-lot scene reportedly required about 700,000 brushstrokes.

news.title: OATs modules turn connected objects into AI Tamagotchis
news.description: OATs modules display expressions generated by Nano Banana on an E Ink screen based on humidity, light, or motion sensors. These devices cost about 20 dollars and are not yet commercially available.

news.title: Agile Robots raises 500 million dollars for its humanoids
news.description: The Munich-based company Agile Robots wants to deploy more industrial robots, particularly in the United States. It raised 500 million dollars from SoftBank and Nvidia to fund its expansion and a possible IPO.

news.title: AI is affecting young workers first, according to an Australian study
news.description: The Reserve Bank of Australia observed a sharper decline in job postings and employment among 15–24-year-olds in occupations highly exposed to AI. The study remains cautious, as the economic cycle and remote work could also explain the trend.

news.title: Tech job postings fall as AI appears in half of listings
news.description: Hacker News’ monthly job-posting thread contains 244 listings in November, 37% fewer than a year earlier. AI appears in 51.6% of postings, while junior roles remain around 3%.

news.title: A developer argues that all AI-generated code should be open source
news.description: Jakub Jankiewicz argues that AI-generated code should be open, since the models were trained on free code and Stack Overflow without permission. He also cites the lack of US copyright protection for works created without human intervention.

news.title: YouTube Music and Spotify’s AI hosts disappoint
news.description: A Wired journalist tested the AI hosts on YouTube Music and Spotify, finding hollow commentary and several errors. She ultimately disabled the feature.

news.title: In Singapore, 94% of small-business owners seek AI help
news.description: According to a YouGov study commissioned by Meta, 94% of surveyed small-business owners in Singapore want more guidance on using AI. Meta trained more than 180 merchants and creators during its Meta Upskill Day 2026.

news.title: Jensen Huang reportedly considering returning as Nvidia’s CEO
news.description: A few days after his resignation linked to the scandal, Jensen Huang reportedly discussed returning to lead Nvidia with associates, according to the Financial Times as reported by Bloomberg. No official confirmation or timeline has been provided.

news.title: Legacy connected devices remain a major network vulnerability
news.description: According to Cisco, nearly 40% of the most exploited vulnerabilities affect end-of-life hardware, including routers and cameras that no longer receive updates. Cisco recommends regularly replacing this equipment, but few brands disclose how long it will be supported.

news.title: Anthropic’s IPO becomes a test for the entire AI sector
news.description: The creator of Claude is set to list on the Nasdaq at between 70 and 78 dollars per share, amid a difficult environment for AI and Nvidia. Anthropic plans to spend more than 900 billion dollars with suppliers despite a 104-billion-dollar loss over nine months.
